To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the asthma patients who have high health literacy, high judgment skills, and high empowerment have better asthma control, more self-efficacy, and better self-management practices.

(1) health literacy and empowerment, but not judgment skills, are positively associated with asthma self-management practices; (2) health literacy is a significant predictor of self-efficacy, which is positively associated with self-management practices.
the asthma patients with higher levels of health literacy and empowerment were more likely to have better judgment skills and to engage in self-management practices.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and validation of a new measure of health literacy, the Test of Functional Health Literacy in Adults (TOFHLA) and the application of this measure to assess the relationship between health literacy and asthma self-management behaviors.

the development of the theory of self-management of health, with particular reference to the self-management of asthma, and the application of the theory to the design and evaluation of interventions.
the influence of health literacy, empowerment, and judgment skills on asthma self-management behaviors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
health literacy is associated with asthma self-management behaviors, and this is mediated by judgment skills and empowerment.
health literacy is a strong predictor of health outcomes.
health literacy, judgment skill, and empowerment are all positively associated with asthma self-management practices, but the strength of association varies by asthma self-management practice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

health literacy, judgment skill, and empowerment are important factors in determining asthma self-management practices and asthma outcomes, and that these factors should be considered when developing interventions to improve asthma self-management.
health literacy, judgment skill, and empowerment are all related to better asthma self-management.
health literacy and judgment skills were associated with asthma self-management practices and empowerment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the relationship between health literacy, asthma self-management practices, and asthma control is not a simple one.

the health literacy, judgment, and empowerment of individuals with asthma are important influences on asthma self-management behaviors, and that these factors are associated with asthma self-management outcomes.
health literacy is a key component of asthma self-management and is associated with asthma self-management practices and health-related quality of life (HRQOL).
